title: The Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1971-04-27
lineage: CD -> Samplitude Professional v11.2 -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of a unique Dead/Beach Boys Fillmore East show—decently clear mix that highlights a smoking “Searchin'” jam and wild renditions of “Okie From Muskogee”/“Johnny B. Goode.”
ai_review.review: The recording is a sound‑board source that sounds clean enough for most listeners, though a few fans note it isn’t as polished as other April ’71 tapes. Musically the show stands out for its unexpected Beach Boys collaboration – “Searchin'” gets a special mention – and Jerry’s ferocious fills on the tongue‑in‑cheek “Okie From Muskogee” and the ensuing “Johnny B. Goode.” Overall the energy is high, with the opening Dead set described as stellar and the novelty jam adding extra excitement.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the performance (especially the Beach Boys collaboration and strong opening set) and rate the recording as good, yielding a combined weighted score in the 4‑star range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and well‑balanced; some listeners prefer other April ’71 sources for cleaner levels but no major dropouts or distortion reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong opening Dead set described as stellar, followed by a novel Beach Boys segment that adds a quirky but exciting twist before returning to classic Dead material.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for ripping “Okie From Muskogee” and delivering scathing fills on “Johnny B. Goode”; noted for strong tone throughout the jam.
band_member_comments.Keys: Theremin highlighted as a notable texture in the performance.
